lists: Learn as You Play Tuned Percussion & Timpani
Play Drum Kit, Timpani & Percussion book 1
exams.syllabus: Trinity Drum Kit & Percussion syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: Initial-G5: 3 pieces/studies 22 each (66; each piece = fluency & accuracy 7 + technical facility 7 + communication & interpretation 8), technical work 14, two supporting tests 10 each (20) = 100. G6-8: same but supporting test 1 = sight reading (10) and test 2 = aural/unpitched aural (drum kit only)/improvisation (10). Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces 22 each (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10) = 100; no supporting tests. Digital repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces/studies at 25 each = 100. Attainment: Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44 (per piece: D 19-22, M 16-18, P 13-15). No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction).

Drum kit: 3 pieces, two from group A (played with Trinity backing track, with or without click) and one from group B (unaccompanied, no click/headphones); max one from Raise the Bar Drum Kit at G1-8; own composition may replace group B piece. Orchestral percussion (combined exam): 3 pieces, one each from tuned percussion, snare drum and timpani lists (no studies); at least one accompanied piece to G5; own composition may replace one. Tuned percussion: 2 pieces + 1 study (digital repertoire-only: 3 pieces + 1 study); at least one accompanied piece to G5; two mallets to G5, G6-8 mallet number marked in list; own composition may replace a piece. Snare drum: 2 pieces + 1 rudimental study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); at least one accompanied piece to G3. Timpani: 2 pieces + 1 study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); accompanied piece required to G5; two drums to G3, G4-8 drums marked in list. Repeats: drum kit observe all; other instruments observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer only. Face-to-face accompaniment must be live from G4 for percussion (recorded allowed to G3, candidate supplies equipment); examiner operates drum kit backing tracks. Own compositions: durations Initial 0.5-1 min rising to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; not marked on compositional quality.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, max 3GB, uploaded via Trinity portal) offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces + technical work + overall performance, no supporting tests) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces, 25 marks each). Digital technical work: exercises (any two of the three listed, not examiner-chosen), tuned percussion scales as Set A or Set B (from memory), snare orchestral figures Set A or B, orchestral extracts G6-8 (two chosen from three). Recorded accompaniment permitted at all grades in digital exams; no headphones/click for technical work or unaccompanied pieces; electric kit allowed to G5 face-to-face.
sections: Scales & technical work

Exercises (all three at trinitycollege.com/percussion-tw; music may be used): sticking patterns, roll development, dynamics. F2F prepare all, candidate picks one, examiner one of remaining; digital: any two. Two drums; rolls clean single-stroke (even unaccented semiquavers allowed to G2).
Sight-reading

Unseen extract, 30 s prep, about two grades lower: Unseen test, 30 s prep, one level below grade: C major, 4/4, f, minims/crotchets/quavers, crotchet rest. On two timpani (Initial-G5), three (G6-8). Face-to-face only.
Aural & other tests

Choose any two of: sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge (10 marks each). Musical knowledge: pitch names, note durations, clefs/staves/bar lines, key and time signatures, basic terms. Aural (piano): 4-bar major melody on piano: clap pulse on 3rd hearing; f or p; legato or staccato; highest or lowest of first three notes. Improvisation on notated rhythmic stimulus (examiner plays twice, 30 s prep to G5, 60 s G6-8): response 2 bars.

Attainment: Distinction 87-100, Merit 75-86, Pass 60-74, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44 (per piece: D 19-22, M 16-18, P 13-15). No need to pass every section. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (pass/merit/distinction).

Drum kit: 3 pieces, two from group A (played with Trinity backing track, with or without click) and one from group B (unaccompanied, no click/headphones); max one from Raise the Bar Drum Kit at G1-8; own composition may replace group B piece. Orchestral percussion (combined exam): 3 pieces, one each from tuned percussion, snare drum and timpani lists (no studies); at least one accompanied piece to G5; own composition may replace one. Tuned percussion: 2 pieces + 1 study (digital repertoire-only: 3 pieces + 1 study); at least one accompanied piece to G5; two mallets to G5, G6-8 mallet number marked in list; own composition may replace a piece. Snare drum: 2 pieces + 1 rudimental study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); at least one accompanied piece to G3. Timpani: 2 pieces + 1 study (repertoire-only: 3 + 1); accompanied piece required to G5; two drums to G3, G4-8 drums marked in list. Repeats: drum kit observe all; other instruments observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer only. Face-to-face accompaniment must be live from G4 for percussion (recorded allowed to G3, candidate supplies equipment); examiner operates drum kit backing tracks. Own compositions: durations Initial 0.5-1 min rising to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; not marked on compositional quality.
None. No theory or lower-grade prerequisite for any grade; grades assume confidence in earlier requirements.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, max 3GB, uploaded via Trinity portal) offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces + technical work + overall performance, no supporting tests) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces, 25 marks each). Digital technical work: exercises (any two of the three listed, not examiner-chosen), tuned percussion scales as Set A or Set B (from memory), snare orchestral figures Set A or B, orchestral extracts G6-8 (two chosen from three). Recorded accompaniment permitted at all grades in digital exams; no headphones/click for technical work or unaccompanied pieces; electric kit allowed to G5 face-to-face.
sections: Scales & technical work

Either (1) exercises: tuning and pitch awareness, sticking and damping, rhythmic independence and tuning; or (2) extracts: Bartok Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta II; Beethoven Sym 9 Molto vivace (F to H); Stravinsky Firebird Infernal Dance (beginning to fig 3). For extracts/exercise lists F2F: prepare all, candidate picks one, examiner one of the rest; digital: choose two.
Sight-reading
Unseen extract, 30 s prep, about two grades lower: Changing metres, wider dynamics/rhythms (any). On two timpani (Initial-G5), three (G6-8). Face-to-face only.
Aural & other tests

Sight reading (10) plus one of aural / improvisation (10). Aural (piano): 8-bar harmonised piece (major or minor): as Grade 6 plus relative key modulation; three changes (pitch in melody only, or rhythm). Improvisation on notated rhythmic stimulus (examiner plays twice, 30 s prep to G5, 60 s G6-8): response 3-4 phrases of 4-8 bars.

w07728.d: Short duet-style piece with accompaniment, themed around a space launch. Practises basic rhythms, pulse and ensemble.
w07728.rw: Shared with timpani and tuned percussion

w07729.d: Short space-themed piece with backing accompaniment. Practises simple rhythms and keeping time with others.

w07750.d: Lively jig with accompaniment, for snare or timpani. Practises compound rhythm and pulse.

w07833.d: Short piece warning about gaps; two-drum tune. Practises moving between two drums.

w07834.d: Short piece sorting out patterns. Practises two-drum patterns and counting.

w07835.d: Short piece imitating bells. Practises basic strokes and even playing.

w07839.d: Waltz with accompaniment for timpani. Practises triple time and moving between drums.

w07840.d: Arrangement of Beethoven themes with accompaniment for timpani. Practises two-drum rhythms.

w07842.d: Contrasting piece with long notes and legato. Practises roll and sustained sound.

w07843.d: Contrasting piece with short, spiky notes. Practises staccato control.

w07844.d: Piece with careful sticking. Practises sticking patterns and drum changes.

w07845.d: Grade 1 timpani study. Practises basic rhythm, tuning and tone.

w07846.d: Bold, loud timpani study. Practises strong tone and dynamics.

w07847.d: March with accompaniment themed on Kiev. Practises march rhythms on timpani.

w07848.d: London tube-stop piece for timpani. Practises moving between drums.

w07849.d: See-saw piece moving back and forth between drums. Practises two-drum alternation.

w07851.d: Arrangement of William Tell Overture finale themes with accompaniment. Practises galloping rhythms.

w07852.d: Timpani piece with German-style title ("Kettledrum Place"). Practises tuning and rhythm.

w07853.d: Grade 2 timpani study. Practises rhythm, tuning and dynamics.

w07854.d: Study with a building-up theme. Practises crescendo and rhythm.

w07855.d: Flight-themed piece with accompaniment for timpani. Practises dynamics and rhythm.

w07856.d: Syncopated 6/8 piece for timpani. Practises compound time and syncopation.

w07858.rw: Useful rudiment practice in a piece

w07862.rw: Good agility exercise as a piece

w07863.d: Rhythmic solo with a strong beat pattern and dynamic contrasts; practises accents and tuning changes.

w07876.d: Fast galloping solo in a driving compound rhythm; builds speed and stick evenness.

w07877.d: Spanish-flavoured solo ("Do you want to dance?") with dance rhythms and syncopation; practises accents and rhythmic character.

w07878.d: Brief study from a primary handbook with simple rhythms and dynamics; practises controlled strokes.

w07879.d: Short study focusing on rhythmic accuracy and dynamic markings; practises control on two or three drums.

w07880.d: Graded study for timpani testing rolls, tuning and rhythmic accuracy at Grade 4 level.

Stanley: Blind English organist and composer, known for organ voluntaries and solos for flute or violin.
Rossini, arr. Faulkner & Obradovic: Italian opera composer, famous for William Tell and The Barber of Seville.
Barratt: Contemporary composer or arranger of graded teaching music for wind instruments.
Caroll: Composer of timpani exercises, etudes and solos.
Beck: American percussionist and composer of snare drum solos.
Joplin, arr. Curnow: American ragtime composer known as the King of Ragtime; Maple Leaf Rag is his most famous work.
Whaley: American percussionist and author of percussion methods.
Faulkner & Obradovic: Authors of graded percussion study collections.
Kamstra: Composer of the timpani piece Rockin' Pauken.
Bomhof: Canadian percussionist and composer of snare drum solos.
Hannickel: Composer of timpani pieces from the 1st Recital Series.
Evans: Contemporary composer of easy saxophone pieces.
Hext: Composer of educational pieces for tuned percussion and timpani.
Carter: Composer of percussion solos including Saëta for timpani.
Aldous, Evans & Pearcey: Trinity percussion team writing educational ensemble pieces for the exam syllabus.
Davila: Composer of accompanied timpani pieces from Timp-Tastic.
Faulkner: Composer of beginner double bass pieces in the First Bass and Second Bass collections published by Recital Music.
Beethoven, arr. Faulkner & Obradovic: Great Classical and early Romantic composer; arranged for timpani.
Pearcey: Composer of Trinity percussion studies and pieces.
Frock: Composer of dance pieces for timpani.
Woud: Dutch timpanist and composer of Symphonic Studies for Timpani.
Schinstine: Composer of the timpani piece Experience in Six.
Rabbio: Composer of contest and recital solos for timpani.
Ukena: Composer of the timpani piece No. 2 Funk.
Ridout: Composer and teacher, writing much church and educational instrumental music.
Houliff: American percussion composer of solo and ensemble works.
